segments.title: Chương 307: 0309 [Tương lai thực sự của Xiaonei.com]
segments.content:
"CEO Chen, the review inquiry period is going to be extended."

"What's the situation?"

"It has to do with the Web 2.0 nature of our company's products. Lately, the SEC review times for all companies primarily focused on Web 2.0 have been extended. There's even a company here in the US that triggered an on-site inspection; the SEC sent people directly to their office to verify documents."

"I understand. I'll have to trouble you to make a few more trips on the US side."

"It's my duty."

Chen Guiliang hung up, feeling a bit helpless. He had encountered a rather unfavorable environment for a public listing.

The roadshow period would probably be extended as well.

A roadshow was all about convincing investors to cough up money. If they had listed under last year's conditions, countless investors would have been clamoring to throw money at them. But now, people were skeptical about Web 2.0, which made fundraising significantly more difficult. They would have to hold several more roadshows.

In the blink of an eye, it was the end of May.

Although they didn't trigger an on-site inspection, the SEC resorted to a transoceanic video conference, which was still quite uncommon at the time. After the video conference, they were asked to submit a jumble of additional materials.

ByteDance's management team gradually grew accustomed to this state of affairs. They went about their daily business as usual, working overtime when new materials needed to be prepared.

"This is this year's graduation season event for Xiaonei." Xie Yang came over with a document.

Chen Guiliang buried his head in the document, reading it carefully.

They were continuing last year's "Digital Graduation Memory Book," which imitated traditional yearbooks. Every user who was about to graduate could apply to the website to generate one. They could also attach and save their graduation photos.

In addition, a "Memory Wall" was automatically generated for each class, where everyone could leave messages.

This year, they had added a "Wishing Tree" and a "Time Capsule."

The "Wishing Tree" was for graduates to make wishes, either with their real names or anonymously, and their classmates could all see their wishes. If a classmate helped them fulfill a pre-graduation wish, a branch of the class's Wishing Tree would light up.

When over 50% of the branches on a graduating class's Wishing Tree were lit, Xiaonei's official staff would certify it and gift all students in that class a virtual commemorative card. Furthermore, the class's Wishing Tree would become dazzlingly brilliant and colorful.

The "Time Capsule" was for graduates to write letters to their future selves or to friends, and they could also include virtual gifts. The letters and gifts would be sealed in the time capsule, and a specific date for opening it could be chosen.

Before that time, no one could open the time capsule, not even the person who wrote the letter.

Once the time came, as long as the user logged into Xiaonei, they would receive a site message to open their time capsule.

Chen Guiliang nodded in approval. "These event ideas are excellent. Who came up with the Wishing Tree and Time Capsule?"

Xie Yang said, "A recent graduate we hired during this year's spring recruitment, named Yang Shiqi."

With the foundation laid by last year's graduation season event, the "Digital Graduation Memory Book" became even more popular this year.

Graduates were ditching traditional paper yearbooks one after another, inviting each other to fill in information in their digital memory books, including names, hobbies, well-wishes, and so on.

The graduation photos they took at school, as well as the class group photos, were all uploaded to their digital memory books.

It wasn't just university students; some high school students also found it trendy and got their classmates to register on Xiaonei to leave each other mementos.

Then, a scene like this unfolded in schools all across the country: the class group photo only existed as a physical print. Students went one by one to their counselors or class advisors, requesting a digital version of the group photo.

Many schools really couldn't produce a digital version; they had used film cameras to take the pictures.

So they came up with other methods: scanning and re-photographing.

As graduation drew closer, the number of new registered users on Xiaonei was increasing every day. These were all graduating students attracted by the commemorative events.

For various reasons, they had never used Xiaonei during their university or high school years, but now they were rushing to register as graduation approached.

"Holy crap, the event has been running for less than half a month, and Xiaonei has gained over a million new users! 800,000 of them are university graduates, and the remaining 300,000-plus are high school graduates."

Xie Yang said, "Although we saw growth last year, it was nowhere near as explosive as this year's."

Chen Guiliang said, "The internet is more widespread now. It's not just a matter of whether you have a computer or access to an internet cafe; students' mindsets and habits have also changed along with it. In the past, you'd buy a yearbook from a store and have every classmate fill it out. Now, it's become asking classmates to visit your own digital memory book. Have the new graduates we hired promote it a bit."

The company didn't hire many recent graduates during spring recruitment. They went to mainstream Tieba forums and online forums to post screenshots of their digital memory books, class wishing trees, and time capsules.

Soon, more graduating students followed suit, posting screenshots to show off.

Netizens who were no longer students watched these posts, their replies tinged with a bit of envy. They didn't have anything like this back in their day.

Chen Guiliang also contacted the "China Youth Daily" and paid a small promotional fee.

The "China Youth Daily" news report came out quickly, with the headline "A New Trend in Graduation in the Internet Age."

The article stated that traditional graduation keepsakes were a thing of the past, and students of the new era had their own new internet-based trends.

The article detailed the content of Xiaonei's graduation events, claiming that not only did graduates love digital mementos, but sharing screenshots online to show them off had also become a popular activity.

"Xiao A from Peking University's Chinese department had a crush on a girl in his class for four years. He never dared to confess because he felt he wasn't good enough. In the end, he made a wish on the class Wishing Tree, hoping to hug her just once. The girl saw his wish and took the initiative to call Xiao A, giving him a hug on graduation day..."

"Xiao A said that this was the most unforgettable moment of his four years in university. He thanked Xiaonei's graduation Wishing Tree for allowing his university life to conclude without regrets..."

"Yuan Chang, a student from Tsinghua University, revealed to our reporter that the time capsule he sealed on Xiaonei contains a letter to his ten-years-in-the-future self. He wrote down his hopes for his future, wishing to have achieved a certain accomplishment in ten years. He couldn't disclose the specific content, but he said he would work hard towards that goal..."

"Liao Shanshan, a student from Renmin University, said she received two time capsules. She doesn't know what's inside or who sent them. She only knows that one can be opened in three years, and the other in five. She is very much looking forward to it..."

Every Xiaonei user could use one time capsule for free. If they wanted a second one, they had to pay, and the gifts sealed inside also cost money. While plain letter paper was free, premium stationery also had to be paid for.

Just from selling time capsules, stationery, and gifts during the graduation season, Xiaonei generated over 6 million yuan in revenue.

Students usually weren't very active in topping up their accounts or sending gifts, but when it came to graduation, they were truly willing to spend!

In this day and age, whenever something new appeared on the internet, traditional media was always keen to pay attention and report on it.

Dozens of media outlets across the country either reprinted the "China Youth Daily" article or wrote a similar one themselves. Surprisingly, it quickly broke out of its circle. Even middle-aged and elderly people who didn't use the internet learned about Xiaonei and its graduation events from the newspapers.

The social impact was enormous!

This was especially true for middle school students about to enter their final year of high school. After hearing the news online or offline, many of them took the initiative to register on Xiaonei.
